topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture series and sets out what students should learn from this lecture.

topics.label: Accumulating genetic and epigenetic changes in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the stepwise accumulation of cellular changes and the questions it raises about cancer development.

topics.label: Cancer as disrupted differentiation and tissue organization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain why understanding cancer requires attention to normal differentiation and tissue architecture rather than isolated tumor cells alone.

topics.label: Distinguishing benign and malignant tumors through invasion and metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how invasion and metastatic spread distinguish malignant tumors from contained benign growths.

topics.label: Benign tumor progression and malignant potential
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine progression from benign growth to invasive malignancy while explaining why benign tumors do not invariably progress or remain harmless.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumor names indicate tissue of origin and malignant status, including exceptions to the naming rules.

topics.label: How cancer causes illness and death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumor growth and metastatic spread impair bodily functions and produce fatal disease.

topics.label: Tumor incidence in humans and other animals
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare the frequency and distribution of tumor types across human populations and animal species.

topics.label: Clinical detection and cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancers can be detected early and why screening effectiveness varies with the tumor and the available test.

topics.label: Lecture close and follow-up
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by directing students to revision, supervision discussions, and upcoming practicals.
